newsitem.title: GERMANY: No sign of German upturn in Q1 - DIW institute.
newsitem.headline: No sign of German upturn in Q1 - DIW institute.

text.p: Germany's economy, burdened by record post-war unemployment and weak industry orders, will shrink by around 1/4 percent in the first quarter of this year, the DIW economic institute forecast on Wednesday.
In a weekly report, the Berlin-based DIW said year-on-year growth would be a modest 1-1/2 percent in the current quarter, with the ex-communist east doing better than the richer west.
"The latest information over industry orders and direction of the unemployment figures show no signs of an uptrend," the DIW report said.
Germany's economy grew 1.4 percent in 1996, but expansion slowed sharply in the fourth quarter, when, the DIW estimates, output rose by just 0.3 percent against the previous quarter.
Industry orders dipped in December by a seasonally-adjusted 1.4 percent, while unemployment surged by half a million to 4.7 million in January -- the highest level since 1933.
New domestic orders had been slack anyway, but export orders -- which had been carrying Germany's modest recovery -- have also started to fall off, hitting the east hardest.
The DIW also said that, with Germany blanketed by snow for much of January, building investment was likely to fall in the current quarter far short of levels seen in late 1996.
